question: Sunil made a paste of rice flour and added a drop of iodine solution to the paste. What will he see?

options.text: The rice flour emits brown fumes

solution:
The correct answer is __**The paste turns blue-black**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When iodine solution is added to a paste of rice flour, the paste turns blue-black.
 
• This color change is due to the presence of starch in the rice flour.
 
• Iodine reacts with the amylose component of starch to form a blue-black complex.
 
• This reaction is a common test for the presence of starch in a sample.
 
• The intensity of the blue-black color can indicate the amount of starch present.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starch:**

 
 
• Starch is a polysaccharide composed of glucose units.
 
• It is commonly found in many plants as a storage form of energy.
 
• Starch consists of two components: amylose and amylopectin.
 
• Amylose is a linear polymer, while amylopectin is branched.
 
• The blue-black color in the iodine test is specifically due to the amylose component.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Solution:**
 
 
• Iodine solution is typically made by dissolving iodine in potassium iodide solution.
 
• It is used as a reagent to detect the presence of starch.
 
• The solution is usually brownish-red but turns blue-black in the presence of starch.
 
 
 
• **Rice Flour:**
 
 
• Rice flour is made by grinding rice grains into a fine powder.
 
• It is commonly used in cooking and baking.
 
• Rice flour contains a significant amount of starch, making it suitable for the iodine test.
 
 
 
• **Other Applications of Iodine Test:**
 
 
• The iodine test is used in food industry to check for starch in products.
 
• It is also used in laboratories for studying plant biology and biochemistry.
